items.quote: Every LightRAG corpus operation (ingest, delete, and the status ops behind GET /corpus, /corpus/counts, /jobs/{job_id} and the /health engine probe) passes run_corpus_op a v1 working_dir derived from the app's store_root and workspace, never the repo-global DEFAULT_V1_WORKING_DIR (v1/.corpus_working_dir).
A document ingested through POST /documents with the default (LightRAG) selector becomes retrievable by POST /query on the LightRAG arms and resolvable by POST /evidence/resolve
The lightrag full-ingest part declares mutates_store (not writes_artifact with scope quarantined), its admission record names the storage it actually writes
Concurrent LightRAG writes to one working dir are serialized: while a LightRAG ingest or delete subprocess is running against a working dir
Adapter input and failures are validated, named and readable: CorpusOpSubprocessError keeps the last 2000 characters of v1 stderr
ingest/delete/status/counts/jobs return a named 'v1 not configured' refusal listing the missing key names (never values), and /health reports degraded with that reason
A LightRAG ingest that exceeds its wall-clock ceiling (900 s ingest, 300 s delete, 60 s status) marks its document as stuck/interrupted
POST /documents/upload (and POST /documents with raw) on the LightRAG path indexes the uploaded file's content
Raw upload inbox files are scoped per workspace (<store_root>/<workspace>/corpus-inbox or equivalent)
IngestJob.enqueued reports the number of documents v1 actually enqueued
